retrieval_observations.easy: scanner::wrap and fold::wrap are each the first source result for the other (about 0.923).
retrieval_observations.medium: queue::wrap is the second source result when querying scanner::wrap (0.786); its queue-based paragraph state is a distinct but visible implementation.
retrieval_observations.hard: shared::split_word reaches fragments::segment only seventh (0.400), despite both partitioning a nonempty Unicode token at a positive scalar boundary. Queue behavior tests exercise segment through public rendering.
retrieval_observations.scheduler: The source-level job-selection and bounded-heap searches return their counterpart only after several type, test, and local-control-flow chunks. The algorithms share the scheduler contract but use distinct working representations.

pairs.rationale: Padding extends one content line to a measured width; border construction creates the top and bottom frame strings.

pairs.equivalence_domain: All documented cowsay fixture inputs.
pairs.contract: Paragraph wrapping and long-word splitting are separate responsibilities.
pairs.rationale: The fold implementation manages whitespace, paragraphs, and line accumulation; split_word is a shared boundary helper for one oversized token.
pairs.difference_witness: Wrapping an ordinary sentence produces multiple word-aware lines without calling split behavior for every word; split_word knows no paragraph boundaries.

pairs.equivalence_domain: All documented cowsay fixture inputs.
pairs.contract: Paragraph wrapping and long-word splitting are separate responsibilities.
pairs.rationale: The scanner implementation controls paragraph and current-line state; split_word only chunks one oversized Unicode word.
pairs.difference_witness: scanner::wrap preserves paragraph breaks and word spacing; split_word receives neither paragraphs nor whitespace context.

pairs.equivalence_domain: All documented cowsay fixture inputs.
pairs.contract: Bubble mode dispatch frames pre-wrapped lines; composed rendering owns the entire message-to-output pipeline.
pairs.rationale: The composed renderer invokes bubble::render after separately clamping width, wrapping the message, and obtaining cow artwork. It does not duplicate bubble framing.
pairs.difference_witness: bubble::render accepts wrapped lines and has no cow output, while composed::render accepts raw text and always appends cow artwork.

pairs.equivalence_domain: All documented cowsay fixture inputs.
pairs.contract: Bubble mode dispatch frames pre-wrapped lines; the pipeline converts raw text and options into the complete cowsay response.
pairs.rationale: render_pipeline delegates one stage to bubble::render and separately controls width, wrapping, cow artwork, and final assembly.
pairs.difference_witness: bubble::render cannot clamp a width or append cow artwork; render_pipeline does both before returning its response.

pairs.equivalence_domain: All documented cowsay fixture inputs.
pairs.contract: Queue wrapping owns paragraph and pending-word state; split_word partitions one Unicode token at a scalar boundary.
pairs.rationale: The queue implementation uses the independently maintained fragments::segment helper for oversize words, while shared::split_word is a different helper used by the scanner and fold implementations.
pairs.difference_witness: queue::wrap consumes complete paragraphs and preserves line boundaries; split_word receives a single token and cannot retain paragraph structure.

pairs.equivalence_domain: All documented cowsay fixture inputs.
pairs.contract: Thought framing renders already-wrapped lines; composed rendering selects a mode after full text layout and appends artwork.
pairs.rationale: The composed path calls generic bubble dispatch rather than maintaining the thought renderer, and it also supports speech output.
pairs.difference_witness: thought::render_bubble always emits parenthesized thought framing; composed::render can render speech and includes a cow.

pairs.equivalence_domain: All documented cowsay fixture inputs.
pairs.contract: Composed rendering assembles a typed rendering request; CLI execution parses argv or stdin and reports malformed options.
pairs.rationale: main::run delegates to the public render dispatcher and owns command-line parsing, input selection, and error conversion; it does not reimplement final assembly.
pairs.difference_witness: An unknown --renderer exits from main::run with an error before a render algorithm is selected, while composed::render only receives valid CowOptions.

pairs.equivalence_domain: Documented scheduler and cowsay inputs.
pairs.contract: Worker selection validates and ranks job records; queue wrapping preserves paragraph text while fitting words into Unicode-scalar-width lines.
pairs.rationale: Both functions consume ordered collections with state, but their validation, working data, output type, and maintenance responsibilities do not overlap in a consolidatable region.
pairs.difference_witness: A ready Job produces its numeric ID through selection, while queue wrapping receives a string and returns formatted text lines.

pairs.equivalence_domain: Documented scheduler and cowsay inputs.
pairs.contract: The bounded heap retains ranked job IDs; the composed renderer prepares wrapped text, frames it, and appends cow artwork.
pairs.rationale: Their collection-building control flow is incidental. One maintains a priority frontier and the other assembles a response string, so no substantial shared maintenance work exists.
pairs.difference_witness: A limit of one can evict lower-priority jobs from the scheduler heap; composed rendering has no job ranking or eviction path and returns a cow response.
